A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SPA and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The complete 25-page v1 and 31-page v3 support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation benchmarks, physical-robot experiments, camera-pose estimation, and representation-learning ablations, with detailed appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds reinforcement-learning, monocular grasp-pose detection, and neural-rendering ablation results in Appendices G-I.

M1.justification: SPA's feature extraction, dynamic volume construction, neural rendering, and losses in Section 2 are unchanged, as are its pre-training procedures. The new MV-MAE decoder is an experimental comparator, not a revision to SPA.

E1.justification: Appendix H adds GraspNet-1Billion and monocular 7-DoF grasp-pose detection, extending robotics task coverage. Existing pre-training datasets and the 268-task suite remain. The five reinforcement-learning tasks reuse existing Meta-World task types; Appendix B's expanded task lists document retained coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix I newly evaluates MV-MAE against SPA, using multiview transformer reconstruction with camera-pose embeddings. Existing comparator sets remain unchanged. RADIO and E-RADIO were already evaluated in v1 Table 7, so the added AM-RADIO summary column does not establish a new comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix G introduces frozen-ViT-B DrQ-v2 reinforcement learning for 1.1 million frames, evaluated through success rates and episode rewards. Appendix H adds grasp-detection training and top-k accuracy evaluation, while Appendix I introduces a matched decoder control. These substantially extend evaluation procedures beyond the retained behavior-cloning protocols.

E4.justification: Appendix I adds a focused test of neural rendering versus multiview attention, controlling the encoder, data, training techniques, and hyperparameters on two VC-1 subsets. Existing dataset, masking, loss-component, SPA-MAE, teacher-model, and spatial-awareness analyses remain; the original hyperparameter ablation is relocated.

E5.justification: Appendix G specifies three seeds for the new RL experiments, and Figure 7 introduces shaded reward-curve variability reporting. Existing seed counts and per-seed results are retained. The new bands are not statistically defined, and no significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Retained main and per-task appendix scores are unchanged. New Tables 9-11 report SPA's RL mean success rate of 0.63 versus MoCoV3's 0.56, grasp accuracy of 31.20 versus MAE's 31.03, and MV-MAE scores of 84.8/59.6 versus SPA's 88.0/61.5 on Meta-World/DMControl. These add substantive findings under new experimental comparisons.

T1.justification: The method equations, Appendix A's rendering-loss definitions, and Appendix E's pose-error formulas match. The added experiments introduce no new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the spatial-awareness hypothesis, neural-rendering-based SPA framework, 268-task/eight-simulator evaluation, and claims of strong embodied performance. The added appendix evidence does not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix I newly interprets the decoder comparison as evidence favoring explicit neural rendering over multiview attention. Appendix G qualifies its RL findings with high variance. Section 7 adds spatial VLM integration as a future application, but retains the now-inconsistent statement that evaluation is restricted to imitation learning.

D1.justification: Appendix B expands task identification, particularly through explicit LIBERO instructions. Appendices G-I provide the new training budget, frozen-encoder settings, implementation references, and MV-MAE construction details. Core SPA hyperparameters, hardware disclosures, and code/model-release commitments remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds a dedicated discussion of 3D robot learning and 3D-aware computer vision, including 3D Diffuser Actor, Yue et al., and HVDistill, and adds NeRF-MAE to the neural-rendering context. References supporting RL, grasp detection, and spatial VLM applications also expand the existing positioning.

P1.justification: The hyperparameter investigation moves from Section 4.1 to Section 5.4. Training-overview and related-work paragraphs are revised, task lists are expanded, and Appendices G-I and acknowledgments are added. Most main-text wording and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is recolored, several tables are compacted and their captions clarified, and the model-summary table gains an AM-RADIO column. v3 adds Tables 9-11 and RL learning curves in Figure 7. Existing plots, the hyperparameter table, and the hardware photograph are relocated without replacing their evidence.

improvement.justification: The matched MV-MAE control tests neural rendering more directly, and the RL and grasp-detection experiments broaden empirical support. Expanded task documentation and related work also help. The gains remain limited: grasp accuracy barely exceeds MAE, RL results have high variance, and Section 7 still incorrectly describes evaluation as imitation-only. Overall, v3 modestly strengthens the unchanged core paper.
